correctness.rationale: At every agent i first pick, any currently available good is a unilateral-deviation lower bound on her realized monotone bundle value. Every j has at most two picks and at most one preceding i, so deleting one j good leaves an empty set or one good available to i; EF1 follows for all n,m<=2n. The exact pure-SPNE continuation recurrence T(S)=max_g min_{Y in E_g(S)} v_i(Y_i) has necessity by off-path SPNE selection and sufficiency by choosing minimizing continuations after deviations. Independent exact 128-mask dynamic recursion with the additive 128*b+binary perturbation gave root masks (13,96,18) and (41,68,18); bad outcome B pays 1092 while any deletion from A leaves >=1161 (gap 69). Finite exhaustive checking is relevant only to the 7-good witness; first-pick argument proves the universal quantifiers.

value.rationale: A natural and sharp first-failure threshold for strategic sequential EF1, lowering the known online-SPNE counterexample from nine to seven goods while proving a two-round safety theorem for all normalized monotone valuations. This is not a mere extra isolated test, and the claim correctly restricts itself to existence of an unfair equilibrium.

final_claim: For fixed cyclic one-good picking, m<=2n guarantees EF1 for every pure SPNE under normalized monotone valuations; for n=3,m=7 strictly positive additive valuations with strict bundle rankings admit an unfair SPNE, establishing the first failure horizon (existential, not every equilibrium).
limitations: One unfair root SPNE of two, not all-equilibria unfairness.
Only normalized monotone valuations and fixed sequential cyclic picking for lower theorem.
residual_risks: Closest SPNE primary full text unavailable, so uninspected appendix could contain a sharper minimality observation.
